chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Halabi from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aslam from him,
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One who kills a believer intentionally, Allah the Exalted will establish upon him all the sins, and the slain one will be cleared of them.'
And this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'I wish that you should bear my sin and your sin, so you would be of the inmates of the fire.'

key_terms.أُرِیدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ: I wish that you should bear

ai.seo_question: What happens to the sins of a murdered believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) elucidates the principle of 'bearing the victim's sins' (hubool ithm al-maqtool), where the intentional killer of a believer assumes the weight of all the victim's sins, while the victim is absolved of his own. This unique jurisprudential concept is grounded in the Quranic verse 11:9, where Prophet Hud invokes a similar burden upon Pharaoh, illustrating how the killer becomes the primary carrier of the victim's spiritual debt.
